sections.text: To those who are always devout and who worship Me with love, I give the power of discrimination, which leads them to Me.
By My grace, I live in their hearts; and I dispel the darkness of ignorance by the shining light of wisdom.
Arjuna asked: Thou art the Supreme Spirit, the Eternal Home, the Holiest of the Holy, the Eternal Divine Self, the Primal God, the Unborn and the Omnipresent.

We had been discussing chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, the Lords Vibhuti, that one which appears to be many is His Vibhuti. By his power of Yoga he appears to us as many. So you go to the jewelry shop, the gold is gold, but the Vibhuti of gold with all the jewelries you see, thats the glory of the gold you see in the jewelry shop.
And the yogic power is the jeweler who is the yogic power, that efficient cause with which he creates many out of this one gold. So Bhagavan said that I am the source of all the beings in this chapter, but says not many people can realize that. Even the Rishis, Maharisis and the Devas Sura Ganaha, even they cannot recognize that.
The reason being that I am the source of even those who we consider to be the higher beings, such as Sura Ganaha and Mahari says, and therefore the effect cannot find its own source. All this Saptarisis, sanat, Kumaras and 14 Manus, theyre all born out of my mind. In other words, anything which you consider is the source of your being, source of your human race or your existence, all came out of me, born out of my mind.
And after that, all the progeny of those are also me. However, it appears to us as many because of our own ignorance about our own self. Now the goal is to unwind that clock from where we started and reached to this point of ignorance and remove that ignorance.
So, Aham Sarvasya Prabhavah, Matta Sarva Pravartate, Iti Matva Bhajante Mam Budhaha Bhava Samanvitaha , but one whose intellect is steady, Bhava Samanvitaha, they will see me as the source of all the beings. Everything is pervaded by me. With such understanding and such devotion, one who worships me, they obviously will get me.
And then: Macchitta Madgat Pranah Bodhayantah Parasparam Kathayantash cha Mam Nityam Tushyanti cha Ramanti cha. What we dont have in our life is contentment and delight. Our life is full of discontent and dejection.
It is often said, our life is like the cardiogram: unhappiness, unhappiness, little happiness, unhappiness, little happiness. Thats the story of our life. What were seeking is exactly the contentment.
I want to be satisfied, I want to be content. I want to have bliss. Then I want to enjoy my life.
Thats what we are looking for. And everything we have tried so far in our life has its own limitation. So that is what we are lacking.
Bhagavan says the only people who achieve this are Macchitaha , those whose mind is absorbed in me. In other words, I have come to the conclusion that the Lord is the source of all being. And we have seen from the logic of spirituality that this world was created by God, using the only material available to him, which is his own self.
You and I cannot be anything different than his own self. With that understanding, if my mind is resting in him always, anything I see, anything I feel, anything I touch is nothing but his self. Machittaha Madgat Pranaha , everything that is happening with my life, my Prana.
Wider view of Prana: any experience which I have through my sense organs is nothing but his experience alone. Because I have come to the firm conclusion that this world could not have been created out of anything but Gods own self. There is no other material available to him to create this world but his own self.
We constantly remind each other that you and I are nothing but the Lords own self. It reminds me of a kind of practical joke. When I was in the Dallas group and a lot of Americans who were involved in what I do, they said, Rajan, I noticed something.
You guys always say, Hari Om. In Chinmaya Mission we meet each other and say, Hari Om. He heard it as hurry home. He said, I know now why you guys have a better family life. You remind each other. You constantly remind each other.
Your wife must be waiting. Rajan, go home, otherwise youll be in trouble. We remind each other, hurry home. Then we wont have any trouble. But the real meaning of Bodhayantaha Parasparam is that we constantly remind each other and enlighten others that there is no other self in you or in me but the same self.
Thats why Namaste means I bow down to you , the same self which is in me is in you. Bodhayantaha Parasparam Kathayantash cha Mam Nityam , constantly speaking about me, constantly reminding ourselves in all our actions that everything happening in my life, every experience that Im experiencing, is nothing but the Lords glory alone. Tushyanti cha Ramanti cha , theyre content and theyre reveling in their own self.
Distinction between Kridanti and Ramanti. Krida requires an outside object to interact with , to play a ball or whatever. Ramanti is reveling in yourself; by yourself youre enjoying.
That is Ramanti. So the two things we always are lacking is this contentment and the joy. Bhagavan said, you can only get by your mind constantly focused on the self.
All your activities are devoted to the self. Reminding, enlightening each other that we are the manifestation of the same Lord. And then Kathayanti cha , speaking about that will lead you to contentment and enjoyment.
Dadami Buddhi Yogam Tam Yena Mam Upayanti Te. Those who do what we have discussed in the previous verse , Bhagawan says, now what is my job? Tesham Satata Yuktanam Bhajatam Priti Purvakam Dadami Buddhi Yogam Tam Yena Mam Upayanti Te. I give them Buddhi Yoga.
Those who are doing what we just discussed , constantly focusing their mind on the self, all their activities dedicated to the self, enlightening each other and speaking about it , theyre content. Because Bhagavan said, I give them Buddhi Yoga. Now, Buddhi Yoga is not this Buddhi that we know as part of Mana, Buddhi, Chitta, Ahankara.
That Buddhi is used to decipher the world of objects. With this intellect I try to decide my experiences , whether this is right or that is right , and I come to a conclusion. So that is the ordinary Buddhi.
But this is Yogic Buddhi. Buddhi we associate with knowing something. Becoming firmly convicted about something is Buddhi.
Waffling is the mind , I like, I dislike. I know, I dont know, this or that. Once I decisively know, thats Buddhi.
In this case, I now decisively know what my self is. There is no doubt left in my mind anymore. Up till now I had a doubt: what is my relationship with the Lord? Is he really looking after me or not? Well, Im doing his puja , does he know that Im doing his puja? Therefore, make sure that we publish it in Bharadwani that I did Lakshmi Puja. Lord, you know that it was published in Bharadwani.
Now its your responsibility. Bhagavan said, I give them that Buddhi which gives you that contentment and joy. Te Yena Mam Upayanti Te. With that Buddhi Yoga they come to me.
Our journey started from when we separated from ourselves by ignorance and started thinking, This is me, this body is me, this mind is me, this intellect is me. And now at my age, I realize that not only this body which I was born with and then grew out of food, but the steel plate in my leg and the acrylic lens in my eye is also me. No difference between the lens I was born with. I actually asked my ophthalmologist. I said, doesnt it come with a lifetime warranty? He said, no, it doesnt.
I said, how about this one? He said, this has a limited warranty too. All that I consider me turns out to be something I have borrowed from this world. Bhagavan said, once that awareness takes place that there is nothing but the self exists.
You know there is nothing but I that exists. That parallax is now removed between my lower self and the higher self. Tesham Eva Anukampartham Aham Ajnana Jam Tamah Nashayami Atma Bhavastho Jnana Dipena Bhasvata.
So now it seems like Bhagavan is doing all that very partially , only for those who put in all this effort. And he really doesnt care about people like us who are constantly busy with our business and our studies and our professions. But Bhagavan is ever compassionate, and all religions say that, including Christianity.
Bhagawan is never considered as one who is harshly judging people. Hes ever compassionate, but he has his own limitations. Unless I seek his compassion, he does not have the power to shower his compassion on me.
Lets say I have five children and four of them never talk to me , only one talks to me. My compassion is only revealed to the one who is constantly with me. The other four have never experienced my compassion because they never allowed me to show it to them.
That sun is always compassionate to give you sunlight. But as long as I keep the windows closed, he doesnt have any power to give you compassion. He has to patiently wait outside your window till you allow him to come inside your room by opening the windows.
Then he can shower his compassion by giving you the light. It is us where we have to become worthy of his compassion. So Bhagawan said, Tesham , those we just talked about, all the qualities they have achieved.
Tesham Eva Anukampartham Aham Ajnana Jam Tamah. What has made me feel different from my own self, from God? My own ignorance. The self is self-effulgent.
It has its own revelation. It becomes revealed to you by its own glory. Myself, Im always aware.
Under whatever condition, I know I exist. That requires no intellectual conviction or intellectual argument about whether I exist or not. Everything else requires my intellectual conclusion.
Am I an architect or a doctor? I come to the conclusion I cannot be anything but an architect. I never went to medical school. So all these things which my upadhi requires , my intellectual conclusion that this is who I am , but I exist requires no intellectual argument.
It reveals to me that I exist, in my awareness. So Bhagavan says, what has removed you from that revelation that yourself and the God-self are one? Your ignorance, created by identification with the non-self , my body, my mind, my intellect , that created an avarana, a veiling, over my understanding that I exist. And that veiling once removed, no other efforts are required.
Good example. Im looking for my key in the room and the key is lying on the table. But the room is pitch dark.
Obviously I cant find my key. But somebody with his compassion turned the lights on. With that compassion of turning the light on, now the light shines on my key and I see my key.
The person didnt have to produce a key. Just out of compassion, he removes the darkness in the room and I find my key. In the same way, Bhagawan said, the self was always dwelling in my own heart.
It is always revealing that I exist. But I consider that I to be this limited I , the existence which I feel all the time, I now take it for granted. It is talking about my body, my mind, my intellect, my achievement, my position, my relationship.
Thats I. Bhagawan said, with the destruction of this ignorance by all the things which we have talked about, I remove that darkness by lighting up the Jnana Dipa, the light of knowledge, in your heart. And you come to this revelation that my existence is of that supreme self.

The Lord makes a remarkable promise here: Dadami Buddhi-yogam tam - I give them the Yoga of discrimination. This is not ordinary intellectual sharpness but a special faculty that connects us back to our source. And crucially, this gift comes to those who worship Priti-purvakam - with love, not mere duty. The image of the sun waiting patiently outside a closed window beautifully illustrates divine grace: it is ever-present, but we must open ourselves to receive it. Gods compassion is unconditional, but our receptivity determines what we experience.
Arjunas response reveals a transformed understanding. He addresses Krishna with profound titles: Param Brahma (Supreme Absolute), Param Dhama (Supreme Abode), Pavitram Paramam (Supreme Purifier), Purusham Shashvatam (Eternal Being), Adi-devam (Primal God), Ajam (Unborn), Vibhum (All-pervading). This is not flattery but recognition - Arjuna has moved from confusion to clarity, from seeing Krishna as merely his friend and charioteer to recognizing him as the Supreme Reality. Such recognition transforms relationship - we cannot treat casually what we truly revere.
Today, practice opening your windows to divine grace. Where have you kept the shutters closed - through doubt, distraction, or simply forgetting? The Buddhi-yoga promised here is not earned through effort alone but received through loving devotion combined with consistent practice. Ask yourself: What would it look like to worship with love rather than obligation? Where in my life am I seeking confirmation from the outside world rather than trusting the light of knowledge that dwells within my own heart?
